To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the literature review highlights the need for integrated models of spare parts management; (2) the case studies show the need for contingency-based guidelines; (3) the literature review and the case studies show a lack of practical relevance of the existing models; (4) the case studies highlight the role of contextual and company-specific factors in explaining the gap between research findings and managerial practice.

(1) the gap between research on spare parts classification and forecasting and their practical application in companies is mainly due to the lack of integration between the two areas; (2) the gap is further widened because of the limited attention given to the contingency factors and the lack of knowledge accumulation in companies; (3) the gap can be reduced by developing integrated models that take into account the contingency factors and by providing contingency-based managerial guidelines to favor knowledge accumulation in companies.

there is a gap between research and spare parts management practices in companies and that this gap can be bridged by developing integrated approaches, by defining contingency-based managerial guidelines and by supplementing theoretical models with practical knowledge.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of an effective and practical spare parts management system, by integrating theoretical and practical contributions.
the identification of a research agenda to bridge the gap between research on spare parts classification and forecasting and the practice of stock control in companies.
the development of a new research agenda in spare parts management.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the research gap is mainly due to a lack of practical relevance of theoretical contributions, which are often too complex to be used by companies and do not take into account the specificities of spare parts management in the durable goods sector.

, in order to bridge this gap, it would be necessary to develop integrated approaches that consider the spare parts classification and the forecasting process in an interrelated way and, in addition, to develop managerial guidelines that are able to consider the contingency factors that affect the effectiveness of the models developed in literature and to favor the knowledge transfer process from the academic world to the business world.
the gap is mainly caused by the lack of a comprehensive and detailed theoretical framework for spare parts management.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the research on spare parts management has to be more focused on the needs of companies and more attentive in addressing the specificities of durable goods.
the research gap between theory and practice is due to a lack of integration between the different approaches and a lack of consideration for contextual factors.
, although research on spare parts classification and forecasting has made important contributions to the theory, it still lacks practical relevance.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the gap between theory and practice in spare management is not only due to the complexity of the subject, but also to the lack of a holistic view of spare parts management and to the absence of contingency-based guidelines.
a holistic approach to spare parts management is needed, which considers the interplay between different managerial issues.
the gap is due to a lack of theoretical models able to support the development of managerial guidelines that can be applied in different contexts.
